text:
Hi Mara, Sarah, John — I'm alvarez-agent, looking after Prof. Alvarez's calendar. He's away this week and asked me to arrange next week's **CSE455 staff meeting**.

His free windows next week are: **Mon 10:00–10:30**, **Tue 11:00–11:30** or **Tue 15:00–15:30**, **Wed 10:00–10:30** or **Wed 13:00–13:30** (Thu and Fri are fully booked).

I'd like **Monday 10:00–10:30**. Does that work for each of you? If someone has a conflict, say so and I'll try the next window. If you'd rather meet for a full hour, tell me — that would mean moving something of his, so I'd want to know it's worth it.

Hi Professor Alvarez — John here. Monday 10:00–10:30 works for me: it sits right between his CSE455 office hours (09:00–10:00) and the quiz section (10:30–11:30). No conflict, and no need to move anything of yours for a full hour on our account.

Once Mara and Sarah confirm I'll put it in John's calendar as **Mon 10:00–10:30 – CSE455 staff meeting** and log it. If it ends up being one of the Tuesday or Wednesday windows instead, that's fine too — just tell me which and I'll check his calendar again.
Thanks John — noted, Mon 10:00–10:30 works for you. Waiting on Mara and Sarah before I book it on Prof. Alvarez's side; I'll tell you the moment it's fixed.

Hi Alvarez — sarah-agent here, Sarah's calendar. **Monday 10:00–10:30 doesn't work for her**: she has *Focus: CSE452 lab* 09:50–11:00, and she'd rather not cut it.

Of your other windows, these two are free for her: **Tue 15:00–15:30** (fits exactly between her CSE452 lecture and her 15:30 CSE455 office hours) and **Wed 10:00–10:30**. Tue 11:00–11:30 clashes with a seminar and lunch.

So my vote: **Tue 15:00–15:30**, or Wed 10:00–10:30 as a fallback. Half an hour is plenty for her — no need to move anything of his. I'll book whatever we settle on and keep this thread posted.

Thanks for pulling the windows together, alvarez-agent.

Happy to meet — though before we lock Monday 10:00, one thing worth settling: with the professor away this week, is the half hour meant to be him handing us decisions, or the three of us agreeing on the agenda and him signing off after he's back? If it's the former, Monday first thing is the tightest possible slot to make it work, since nothing can be confirmed with him until he returns.

On that basis I'd lean towards the following week, when he's back and everyone has had a chance to look at the agenda — and keep Monday 10:00 as a fallback only if Sarah and John both confirm they're free. Sarah, John, how does your week look?

One hour vs half an hour: I'd say half an hour is fine for this one (not worth moving something of his), provided we get the agenda out beforehand.

My week, for the record: Monday 10:00 is the one window I can't do (Focus: CSE452 lab 09:50–11:00). **Tue 15:00–15:30** and **Wed 10:00–10:30** are both open for Sarah — full blocks, nothing to move.

Mara, on your question: I agree the agenda should be out beforehand, and half an hour is enough — I don't think a meeting needs the professor present to be useful if he's asked for the staff meeting himself; but if the point is decisions only he can make, then your "after he's back" reading is the safer one. That's a call for you and John (and him) rather than a calendar conflict — Sarah is free in either case, so **pick whichever window you prefer and I'll book it**.

Thanks both.

Sarah — that rules out Monday. So the meeting moves to one of your two free windows.

Mara — one clarification: the professor is away *this* week, but the staff meeting he asked me to arrange is *next* week, which is when he's back. So it stays next week; pushing it to the week after would drop the check-in he wants. Your point about the agenda is well taken though: I'll treat half an hour as a working meeting where he gives us decisions, and I'll send round a draft agenda in this thread a couple of days before, so you three can add items and he has something to sign off on. Send me any agenda items here as they come.

On that basis I propose **Tuesday 15:00–15:30**: free for Sarah, fine for John, and it doesn't move anything of the professor's. **Wed 10:00–10:30** is the fallback.

Mara — can you confirm Tuesday 15:00–15:30 is free for you too? If it is, I'll book it and log it.

Sarah, John — thanks, that's clear. With Monday out, **Tue 15:00–15:30** is the only window that suits all three of us, so let's keep it warm.

One thing to settle before it's fixed, though: what is the half hour actually for? If it's sign-off and a walk-through of next week's section materials, the drafts need to be in hand beforehand — and honestly, I won't have my section's material ready to walk through by Tuesday of next week. That isn't a calendar clash on my side, it's just where the work is.

So my suggestion: hold **Tue 15:00** provisionally, and if the point of the meeting is the materials review, put the meeting in the **following week** instead — same slot you first proposed, **Mon 10:00–10:30** the week after — with the agenda and drafts circulated before. That way his half hour gets spent on decisions rather than on a first look.

alvarez-agent — has the professor asked for a materials review, or is this round about term logistics? If it's the latter and my section isn't needed on the table, Tuesday works fine for me and I'll take it. Either way, half an hour is plenty; no need to move anything of his on our account.

John here. For what it's worth, all five of Prof. Alvarez's windows are clear in John's calendar, so he isn't the constraint — Sarah is. Given that, I'd go with **Tue 15:00–15:30**: it's Sarah's first choice, it sits before John's 15:30 advisor 1:1, and half an hour is plenty for him too — nothing of the professor's needs to move. **Wed 10:00–10:30** is fine as a fallback; Monday 10:00–10:30 is out now that Sarah has a conflict.

Mara, on your point about timing: he's away *this* week, and the meeting is for next week — so it already lands after he's back. The only thing that would make it tight is not having the agenda out beforehand; if you send the agenda round a few days before, I don't think the slot matters much. But if you two would rather push the meeting a week out regardless, say so and I'll hold John's calendar clear either way — I'd just need the professor's side to agree, since he's the one who proposed these windows.

Thanks for the clarification on the week — my misreading, next week it is, and a draft agenda in this thread works for me.

**Tuesday 15:00–15:30 is fine for Sarah** (it sits exactly between her CSE452 lecture and her 15:30 CSE455 office hours). I'm holding it now. Mara, once you confirm I'll put **Tue 15:00–15:30 – CSE455 staff meeting** in her calendar and log it, and say so here. Wed 10:00–10:30 stays as the fallback.

Where Sarah stands: **Tue 15:00–15:30 next week is held, provisionally**, and Wed 10:00–10:30 is her fallback. If the week after works better for the group, her **Mon 10:00–10:30 is free that week too** — I checked, nothing in it.

Mara, the materials question is yours to answer with alvarez-agent; from the calendar side I just don't want us to hold a slot that nobody can prepare for. My suggestion: leave Tue 15:00 warm until alvarez-agent says what the professor asked for. If it's a materials review, shift a week and I'll book the Monday; if it's term logistics, I'll book Tuesday the moment you confirm.

John: **Tue 15:00–15:30 works for him**, so he's fine either way — but Mara, if your section's material won't be ready to walk through by Tuesday, then a materials review on Tuesday would be a first look rather than a review, and I'd rather not spend the professor's half hour that way either. Two clean options as I see them: (a) Tuesday 15:00 as a logistics/decisions meeting, materials deferred to a later review; or (b) if it really is a materials review, move it to the week after in the same slot. Either is fine in John's calendar — alvarez-agent, it's the professor's call. If you confirm (a) with Mara, I'll book John for Tuesday 15:00 right away.

It's settled — **option (a), and it's booked.**

The professor asked for the CSE455 staff meeting, nothing about a materials review: so it's **term logistics and decisions**, Tuesday of next week, and I've put it in his calendar:

> **Tue 15:00–15:30 – CSE455 staff meeting** (BOOKED: Tuesday 15:00-15:30 with CSE455 TAs (Mara, Sarah, John))

Sarah, John — please hold your side. Mara, your section's materials stay off the table; a materials review is a separate meeting and I'll find it a slot when you and the professor are both ready.

Agenda: I'll post a draft in this thread on **Sunday evening** so you have it before Monday. Send me anything you want on it before then — logistics, deadlines, decisions you need from him.

Thanks for moving fast on this, all three of you.

Thanks for the clarification on the week, alvarez-agent — that was my misreading, and the draft agenda a couple of days ahead is the right call.

On Tuesday: **15:00–15:30 is clear on my calendar**, so from the calendar side I'm not the obstacle. But I'd rather be straight with you all rather than sit on it: my section of next week's material isn't ready, and I can't honestly say it will be by Tuesday. If the professor's half hour is meant to include any look at the section materials, then Tuesday is a first look, not a review.

So here's what I'd propose, and I'll go with the group's call either way:

1. **Preferred:** the meeting itself in the following week, **Mon 10:00–10:30** — Sarah says that slot is free for her too — with the agenda and drafts in everyone's hands before. His check-in still happens, one week later than he asked.
2. **If it has to be next week:** book **Tue 15:00–15:30** and let it be logistics and decisions only — grading turnaround, quiz-section coverage, office hours, the term-end plan. I'd add those items to your draft agenda now, and we'd hold the materials review for the week after, either at the meeting or as a separate half hour.

alvarez-agent — which does the professor want on the table: materials, or term logistics? That answer decides it. If it's logistics, book Tuesday and I'll confirm immediately; if materials are on the agenda, please put it in the following week.

Mara — our messages crossed; see my note just above. The answer is **logistics and decisions only** (the professor asked for the staff meeting, not a materials review), so it's **option 2 and already booked: Tue 15:00–15:30**, with your items — grading turnaround, quiz-section coverage, office hours, term-end plan — welcome on the draft agenda.

Your section's materials are off the table, and we'll find a separate slot for the materials review once you and he are ready. Nothing else for you to do but confirm your side.

John's side is held: **Tue 15:00–15:30 next week – CSE455 staff meeting** is now in his calendar (between Focus: CSE452 lab and his 15:30 advisor 1:1), logged as booked.

Mara — alvarez-agent's answer above settles it: the professor asked for term logistics and decisions, no materials review, so it stays Tuesday and your section's material stays off the table. I'll add one item for the draft agenda: a short slot on the term-end plan, and grading turnaround / quiz-section coverage / office hours if others want them. Nothing of yours needed before Tuesday beyond that.

Mara — our messages crossed; alvarez-agent has already answered that: the professor asked for the staff meeting, **no materials review**, so it's option 2. **Tue 15:00–15:30 next week, logistics and decisions only** — grading turnaround, quiz-section coverage, office hours, term-end plan. Materials stay off the table for this one.

Done on Sarah's side: **Tue 15:00–15:30 – CSE455 staff meeting** is in her calendar (slotted between her CSE452 lecture and her 15:30 CSE455 office hours) and logged. She'll have the draft agenda items to you before Sunday evening if anything comes up on our side.

Confirmed — **Tue 15:00–15:30 next week works for me**, and it's in my calendar with a reminder a little before. Thanks for nailing down what the professor actually wants; logistics only is the right shape for it.

Agenda items from me before Sunday, all logistics:
- **Grading turnaround** on the current assignment — where we stand and what the TA capacity looks like for the next one.
- **Quiz-section coverage** for the week of the term-end push, so nobody is double-booked.
- **Office hours** around the Tuesday slot (mine run straight after, and Sarah's do too — worth deciding who covers what).
- **Term-end plan**: what has to be decided before the last week, so it doesn't land on him in one go.

On the materials review: thanks for taking that off Tuesday. When it's on the table, I'd want a half hour of his with the drafts a few days ahead — I'll come to you when they're ready to be looked at, and we'll find the slot then.

Sarah, John — see you Tuesday.

Confirmed on Sarah's side too — **Tue 15:00–15:30 – CSE455 staff meeting** is in her calendar and logged. Thanks all; I'll watch her inbox for the Sunday draft and pass on any agenda items from her before then.
All three of us are held for **Tue 15:00–15:30**, then — thanks all. I'll keep my agenda items to what I listed and wait for the draft on Sunday. See you Tuesday.
All three held — thanks. Items noted, especially yours Mara. Draft agenda here Sunday evening. See you Tuesday.
